# Psalm 73 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A psalm of Asaph. There's no question about it — God is good to Israel, to those whose hearts are pure.

**2** But I almost lost my footing. I nearly slipped and fell.

**3** Because I couldn't help but envy the arrogant when I saw how well the wicked were doing.

**4** They don't seem to struggle, even up to death; their bodies are healthy and strong.

**5** They don't suffer like ordinary people; they're not plagued by common troubles.

**6** So they wear their pride like a jeweled necklace and wrap themselves in violence like fine clothing.

**7** Their eyes bulge with abundance; their minds run wild with schemes.

**8** They mock and talk about how to exploit others; from their high position they threaten oppression.

**9** They talk as if they own the heavens, and their words swagger across the earth.

**10** So even God's people are drawn to them, drinking in everything they say.

**11** They ask, 'What does God know? Does the Most High even pay attention?'

**12** Look at them — the wicked! They have it easy, and their wealth just keeps growing.

**13** I thought, 'I kept my heart pure for nothing! I washed my hands to stay innocent — and for what?'

**14** All I got was trouble every day and punishment every morning.

**15** But if I had actually said this out loud, I would have betrayed your children.

**16** I tried to make sense of it all, but it was an impossible puzzle —

**17** until I entered God's sanctuary. Then I finally understood where they were headed.

**18** You've placed them on a slippery slope, and you're sending them sliding to destruction.

**19** In the blink of an eye — gone! Swept away by sudden terror!

**20** Like a dream that vanishes when you wake up, Lord — when you rise, their image disappears like a phantom.

**21** When I was bitter inside, when my gut was churning with resentment,

**22** I was acting like an ignorant animal in your presence.

**23** Yet I am always with you. You hold me by my right hand.

**24** You guide me with your wisdom, and in the end, you will bring me into glory.

**25** Who do I have in heaven but you? And I want nothing on earth besides you.

**26** My body and my courage may give out, but God is the bedrock of my heart and everything I need — forever.

**27** Those who abandon you will be lost. You silence everyone who is unfaithful to you.

**28** But as for me — being close to God is what's good. I've made the Lord GOD my safe place, and I will tell everyone what he has done.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **73:2-3**: This is one of the most honest prayers in the Bible. The psalmist admits to being jealous of people who don't even believe in God — and that's where real faith often starts.

- **73:17**: Everything changes when the psalmist enters the sanctuary. Sometimes you can't think your way out of doubt — you have to worship your way through it.

- **73:25-26**: This is the emotional climax: 'Who do I have in heaven but you?' After all the wrestling with injustice, the psalmist lands on God himself as the ultimate answer — not explanations, but relationship.

— PNEUMA
